holidays.name: National Roast Leg of Lamb Day
holidays.description: A day for carving into a juicy roast leg of lamb, usually studded with garlic and rosemary and served with mint sauce or jelly. It's a good excuse to haul out the good carving knife.
holidays.origin: The origins are unclear. Like many American food days, it was likely promoted by food enthusiasts and meat industry groups. Lamb has long been a springtime centerpiece in Easter and Passover traditions.
holidays.funFact: Lamb has been eaten for thousands of years, and mint sauce became a classic pairing in England, where the herb's sharpness helped cut through the richness of the meat.

holidays.name: National Cosmopolitan Day
holidays.description: A toast to the pink, citrusy cocktail made with vodka, triple sec, cranberry juice, and lime juice. Raise a martini glass and pretend you're in a 90s TV show.
holidays.origin: An unofficial drink holiday, observed by bartenders and cocktail fans. The drink rose to fame in the late 1980s and 1990s, and its popularity was boosted by its appearance on Sex and the City.
holidays.funFact: Bartender Toby Cecchini is widely credited with creating the modern version of the Cosmopolitan in New York City in the late 1980s, using Absolut Citron and fresh lime juice.

holidays.name: National Totally Hammered Day
holidays.description: A day dedicated to the hammer, the most basic of tools, and to nailing down those DIY projects. Despite the cheeky name, it's about the hammer, so no judgment.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial, tongue-in-cheek observance that plays on a double meaning of the word 'hammered.' It's celebrated by hardware enthusiasts and punsters.
holidays.funFact: Hammers are among the oldest tools known to humans. Early hammers were simply stones, and archaeologists have found hammerstones that are around 3 million years old.

holidays.name: Public Radio Day / Tuesday Dedicated Awareness: Space Day (First Friday in May)
holidays.description: Not exactly on the 7th every year, but this stretch of early May is full of space and science celebrations. On May 7, stargazers and radio fans alike can tune in to the airwaves and the cosmos.
holidays.origin: Radio history is tied to May 7, 1895, when Russian scientist Alexander Popov demonstrated his radio receiver to the Russian Physical and Chemical Society. Russia celebrates Radio Day on this date.
holidays.funFact: Russia still celebrates Radio Day every May 7 in honor of Popov's 1895 demonstration, even though Guglielmo Marconi gets most of the credit in the West.

holidays.name: Great American Meatout Alternative: National Barefoot Day
holidays.description: A day to kick off your shoes and let your toes breathe. Wiggle them in the grass, the sand, or on your living room carpet.
holidays.origin: Barefoot celebrations are informal and unofficial, popularized by outdoor lovers, wellness bloggers, and foot-care fans who argue that walking barefoot strengthens the feet and improves balance.
holidays.funFact: The human foot has 26 bones, 33 joints, and more than 100 muscles, tendons, and ligaments, so it's a lot more complicated than it looks.
